en: The Apadāna of the Elder Kadambapupphiya Bandhujīvaka Chapter, Number 6 I am a follower of the Buddha, the Teacher, the One with Vision, Who has crossed over the flood and reached the further shore. Having heard his teaching, I have attained the fruit of stream-entry; I shall not be subject to rebirth in the womb for a seventh time. In the past, when the Buddha Kassapa was in the world, I was a merchant who lived in Benares. At that time, the Teacher, the Great Sage, Was traveling through the Kosala country. I went forth from my home to follow him, And I became a monk under the Great Sage. I took up my residence in a forest grove, And there I practiced meditation on the foul. For twenty thousand years I remained there, Constantly practicing meditation on the foul. Then, having passed away from that human life, I was reborn in the realm of the Thirty-Three. There I dwelt for eighty-four thousand years, Enjoying celestial pleasures. From there, passing away, I was reborn among humans, And I attained the fruit of non-returning. Now I dwell in the realm of Tusita, A god of great power and majesty. When the Teacher, the Great Sage, appears in the world, I shall go forth as a monk under him. Having become a monk under the Great Sage, I shall attain the final Nibbāna. This is my last birth in the realm of existence; I shall not be subject to further rebirth. Thus did the Elder Kadambapupphiya speak Of his own former deeds. One who hears this account of the Elder’s life Will attain the fruit of stream-entry.
Not far from the Himālaya is a mountain named Kukkuṭa;
at the foot of that mountain,
Those seven Buddhas dwell there.
Having seen the kadamba tree in full bloom,
rising up like the king of lamps;
Taking them up with both hands,
I scattered them over the seven Buddhas.
Ninety-four aeons ago,
Because I offered that flower,
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of worshiping the Buddha.
In the ninety-second aeon from now,
there were beings named Puppha;
they were endowed with the seven treasures.
Universal monarchs of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the Venerable Elder Kadambapupphiya recited these verses.
This is the sixth legend of the Elder Kadambapupphiya.
